gold_assessment.reasoning: Chief complaint and HPI generated facts (cc-001, hpi-001) both describe shortness of breath worsening over the last ~2 weeks; they add detail about worsening in the last few days but are consistent with a 2‑week history that has been worsening.

Generated hpi-002 states breathless on minimal exertion, and there is no generated statement saying SOB at rest; this aligns with ‘more SOB on minimal exertion, nil SOB at rest’. Partial but accurate coverage.
Generated hpi-007 and hpi-008 (and ros-002, ros-003) document denial of chest pain and palpitations; this matches the gold denial of chest pain/palpitations.
Generated hpi-004 and ros-001 both describe a mild dry cough; this is consistent with an associated mainly dry cough.
Generated hpi-009 and ros-005 document denial of fevers; this matches the gold ‘No fevers.’
Generated hpi-005 notes swelling in both ankles starting a few days ago; this corresponds to bilateral ankle edema over the past few days.

Generated hpi-006 mentions prior heart failure; pmh-001 and meds (med-001, med-004) confirm heart failure history and current furosemide use. Although the diuretic class is not explicitly stated, furosemide is a loop diuretic, so the concept is covered.

Gold explicitly states urinary polyuria as a symptom; generated ros-006 reframes this as increased urination since starting medications without clarifying large volume output, and attributes it to medication rather than as a presenting urinary symptom. The specific polyuria symptom as in HPI is not clearly captured.

Generated pmh-001 supports history of heart failure but generated pmh-002/asm-002 describe a prior myocardial infarction (small heart attack). The gold fact is ‘?unstable angina’ (uncertain unstable angina), not MI. This is not supported and is instead altered, so the ‘possible unstable angina’ component is omitted.

Gold lists furosemide, aspirin, simvastatin. Generated med-001 and med-002 confirm furosemide and aspirin but replace simvastatin with bisoprolol (med-003). Thus, furosemide and aspirin are covered; simvastatin is omitted and bisoprolol is an added, non‑gold medication.
Generated allergy-001 states no known drug allergies, matching NKDA.
Generated fh-001 states father died of a heart attack in early sixties; this matches father died of MI in his early 60s.
Generated fh-002 states mother has osteoporosis; extra detail that she is alive is an addition but consistent. Core fact is covered.
Generated sh-001 states lives alone with two cats; naming the cats is added detail. Core content matches.
Generated sh-002 states works part‑time as a lorry driver; additional notes about only daytime shifts and exhausting work are additive but consistent.
Generated sh-003 and sh-004 describe a former smoker, about one pack per day for 25 years, quit time not specified; this matches a 25‑pack‑year history and ex‑smoker status.
Generated sh-005 confirms no alcohol consumption, consistent with ‘No etOH.’
Generated asm-001 explicitly identifies decompensated/exacerbation of heart failure with corresponding symptoms; this aligns with ‘Imp: exacerbation of heart failure.’
Generated med-004 and plan-001 both state increasing furosemide from once daily to twice daily; this reflects ‘Increase furosemide BD.’
Gold requests U&Es, FBC, BNP. Generated plan-002 mentions full blood count and renal function (i.e., FBC and U&Es) but omits BNP. Thus FBC and U&Es are covered; BNP is omitted.
Generated plan-003 and plan-010 both include scheduling/obtaining an echocardiogram; this matches ‘Arrange echo.’
Generated plan-005 and fu-001 specify follow‑up in one week; equivalent to review in 7 days.

Gold: earlier review if worsening symptoms including chest pain, SOB, dizziness. Generated plan-004 and plan-008/fu-002 advise contacting provider/report worsening symptoms, listing chest pain, palpitations, dizziness; SOB is not explicitly mentioned, and palpitations is added. Thus the early‑review instruction is covered, but specific inclusion of worsening SOB is omitted.
